title: devexp-sync-notes-apr-15-2026
content:
Attendees: Priya Nair (owner), Mark Robinson, Zoe Kim, Miguel Torres, Emma Chen, Samir Patel (joined late)

Date: 2026-04-15 weekly sync (DevEx)
Location: #devexp Slack / Zoom
Duration: 45m

Agenda:
- Quick status: SDK releases (Python / TS)
- Docs site migration & search regressions
- Quickstarts & sample apps status (Next.js Edge + Serverless templates)
- Open blockers and rollout plan for beta customers
- Action items and owners

Summary / Highlights:
1) Python SDK 1.4.0-beta rollout
- Miguel: published 1.4.0-beta to test-orgs; includes streaming refactor and a small breaking change in how retry metadata is surfaced (see PR #1241).
- Early feedback: two partners reported a change in stream event ordering when reconnecting. Mark is triaging.
- Decision: hold GA until we land patch for reconnection ordering or add a compatibility flag.

2) TypeScript SDK generator issues
- Zoe: generator now emits more precise types for function/tool-calling signatures, but broke a handful of legacy sample apps because of stricter discriminated unions.
- Short-term: we will publish a migration guide in docs and keep a legacy compatibility build for one release cycle.
- Jira: DX-237 created to track generator follow-ups.

3) Docs site migration (Docusaurus v3 -> internal search)
- Priya: migration branch exists, search index differences noticed — several quickstart pages not surfacing for common queries ("nextjs quickstart", "edge functions").
- Cause: frontmatter changes and tag normalization. Emma found a missing tag mapping for "edge" -> "edge-functions".
- Action: Emma to push mapping fix; Zoe to run local index and sanity-check top 50 queries by Friday.

4) Quickstarts and sample apps
- Current focus: Next.js Edge quickstart (target: low-latency demo) and a minimal Flask example for Private deployments.
- Samir: Next.js example now uses streaming + edge invocation, but needs updated environment variable instructions for the new API key scoping model.
- Unresolved: how to show Dedicated vs Hosted routing in demo UI without exposing billing details. Idea: mock a "routing tier" toggle and document expected latency/cost delta.

5) Internal rollout & beta customers
- Pilot customers: two startups on Hosted API are testing new samples. One enterprise beta requested Private quickstart with explicit KMS setup steps.
- Priya: add a short enterprise appendix for Private (KMS/HSM notes, minimal network diagram).

6) Observability + samples integration
- Request from Solutions Eng: add a small snippet to samples showing how to parse per-token latency metrics from the SDK (token-level metrics shipped in SDK 1.4.0).
- Mark will prototype and add to the chatbot-sample repo.

Blockers / Risks:
- Streaming reconnection ordering (high) -> blocks GA of Python SDK 1.4.0
- TS generator strict types causing consumer breakage (medium) -> possible churn for users updating quickly
- Docs search regressions could make quickstarts hard to find (medium)
- Private quickstart KMS complexity (low/medium) -> need SME review from security team

Decisions Made:
- Hold Python SDK GA until reconnection ordering fix or compatibility flag landed. (owner: Miguel)
- Publish TS generator migration guide and ship legacy build for one release (owner: Zoe)
- Add enterprise appendix to Private quickstart (owner: Priya)

Action Items (owner / ETA):
- Miguel: debug reconnection ordering, aim for patch by 2026-04-18 (JIRA: DX-241).
- Mark: prototype token-level metrics snippet and submit PR to chatbot-sample by 2026-04-20 (GH: /chatbot-sample PR TBD).
- Emma: push docs tag mapping fix and re-run search index by 2026-04-16.
- Zoe: draft TS migration guide + examples for discriminated unions by 2026-04-19.
- Priya: write Private quickstart appendix (KMS + network sketch) by 2026-04-21 and request security SME review.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Consider adding a small "compatibility" section at top of quickstarts highlighting known breaking changes between SDK minors; saves time when users hit friction.
- Could wire a lightweight telemetry event in sample apps to anonymously report which quickstart was used (opt-in) — helps prioritize docs. Check privacy + legal.
- Re: Dedicated vs Hosted demo — maybe onboard a small synthetic load generator to show latency curves without exposing real billing.

Follow-ups / Next sync:
- Next DevEx weekly: 2026-04-22, same channel.
- Miguel to post interim status in #devexp and tag Priya + Mark if patch is delayed.

Linked artifacts / refs:
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1241
- Jira: DX-237 (TS generator follow-ups)
- Jira: DX-241 (Python streaming reconnection)
- Confluence draft: DevExp/Quickstarts (internal)

Status: draft — want to capture quick timestamps and action ownership before we publish a cleaned-up weekly summary in the team newsletter.

-- end of notes --
